Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# The Silver Searcher

A code searching tool similar to `ack`, with a focus on speed.

## What's so great about Ag?

* It is an order of magnitude faster than `ack`.
* It ignores file patterns from your `.gitignore` and `.hgignore`.
* If there are files in your source repo you don't want to search, just add their patterns to a `.ignore` file. (\*cough\* `*.min.js` \*cough\*)
* The command name is 33% shorter than `ack`, and all keys are on the home row!

Ag is quite stable now. Most changes are new features, minor bug fixes, or performance improvements. It's much faster than Ack in my benchmarks:

    ack test_blah ~/code/  104.66s user 4.82s system 99% cpu 1:50.03 total

    ag test_blah ~/code/  4.67s user 4.58s system 286% cpu 3.227 total

Ack and Ag found the same results, but Ag was 34x faster (3.2 seconds vs 110 seconds). My `~/code` directory is about 8GB. Thanks to git/hg/ignore, Ag only searched 700MB of that.

## Installing

### macOS

    brew install the_silver_searcher

or

    port install the_silver_searcher


### Linux

* Ubuntu >= 13.10 (Saucy) or Debian >= 8 (Jessie)

        apt-get install silversearcher-ag
* Fedora 21 and lower

        yum install the_silver_searcher
* Fedora 22+

        dnf install the_silver_searcher
* RHEL7+

        yum install epel-release.noarch the_silver_searcher
* Gentoo

        emerge -a sys-apps/the_silver_searcher
* Arch

        pacman -S the_silver_searcher

* Slackware

        sbopkg -i the_silver_searcher

* openSUSE

        zypper install the_silver_searcher

* CentOS

        yum install the_silver_searcher

* NixOS/Nix/Nixpkgs

        nix-env -iA silver-searcher

* SUSE Linux Enterprise: Follow [these simple instructions](https://software.opensuse.org/download.html?project=utilities&package=the_silver_searcher).


### BSD

* FreeBSD

        pkg install the_silver_searcher
* OpenBSD/NetBSD

        pkg_add the_silver_searcher

### Windows

* Win32/64

  Unofficial daily builds are [available](https://github.com/k-takata/the_silver_searcher-win32).
  
* winget

        winget install "The Silver Searcher"
  
  Notes:
  - This installs a [release](https://github.com/JFLarvoire/the_silver_searcher/releases) of ag.exe optimized for Windows.
  - winget is intended to become the default package manager client for Windows.  
    As of June 2020, it's still in beta, and can be installed using instructions [there](https://github.com/microsoft/winget-cli).
  - The setup script in the Ag's winget package installs ag.exe in the first directory that matches one of these criteria:
     1. Over a previous instance of ag.exe *from the same [origin](https://github.com/JFLarvoire/the_silver_searcher)* found in the PATH
     2. In the directory defined in environment variable bindir_%PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE%
     3. In the directory defined in environment variable bindir
     4. In the directory defined in environment variable windir
  
* Chocolatey

        choco install ag
* MSYS2

        pacman -S mingw-w64-{i686,x86_64}-ag
* Cygwin

  Run the relevant [`setup-*.exe`](https://cygwin.com/install.html), and select "the\_silver\_searcher" in the "Utils" category.

## Editor Integration

### Vim

You can use Ag with [ack.vim](https://github.com/mileszs/ack.vim) by adding the following line to your `.vimrc`:

    let g:ackprg = 'ag --nogroup --nocolor --column'

or:

    let g:ackprg = 'ag --vimgrep'

Which has the same effect but will report every match on the line.

### Emacs

You can use [ag.el][] as an Emacs front-end to Ag. See also: [helm-ag].

[ag.el]: https://github.com/Wilfred/ag.el
[helm-ag]: https://github.com/syohex/emacs-helm-ag

### TextMate

TextMate users can use Ag with [my fork](https://github.com/ggreer/AckMate) of the popular AckMate plugin, which lets you use both Ack and Ag for searching. If you already have AckMate you just want to replace Ack with Ag, move or delete `"~/Library/Application Support/TextMate/PlugIns/AckMate.tmplugin/Contents/Resources/ackmate_ack"` and run `ln -s /usr/local/bin/ag "~/Library/Application Support/TextMate/PlugIns/AckMate.tmplugin/Contents/Resources/ackmate_ack"`

## Other stuff you might like

* [Ack](https://github.com/petdance/ack3) - Better than grep. Without Ack, Ag would not exist.
* [ack.vim](https://github.com/mileszs/ack.vim)
* [Exuberant Ctags](http://ctags.sourceforge.net/) - Faster than Ag, but it builds an index beforehand. Good for *really* big codebases.
* [Git-grep](http://git-scm.com/docs/git-grep) - As fast as Ag but only works on git repos.
* [fzf](https://github.com/junegunn/fzf) - A command-line fuzzy finder 
* [ripgrep](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep)
* [Sack](https://github.com/sampson-chen/sack) - A utility that wraps Ack and Ag. It removes a lot of repetition from searching and opening matching files.

## Documentation

For detailed usage information and command-line options, see the manual page in the `doc/` directory.

  * `-B --before [LINES]`:
    Print lines before match. If not provided, LINES defaults to 2.

  * `--[no]break`:
    Print a newline between matches in different files. Enabled by default.

  * `-c --count`:
    Only print the number of matches in each file.
    Note: This is the number of matches, **not** the number of matching lines.
    Pipe output to `wc -l` if you want the number of matching lines.

  * `--[no]color`:
    Print color codes in results. Enabled by default.

  * `--color-line-number`:
    Color codes for line numbers. Default is 1;33.

  * `--color-match`:
    Color codes for result match numbers. Default is 30;43.

  * `--color-path`:
    Color codes for path names. Default is 1;32.

  * `--column`:
    Print column numbers in results.

  * `-C --context [LINES]`:
    Print lines before and after matches. Default is 2.

  * `-D --debug`:
    Output ridiculous amounts of debugging info. Not useful unless you're actually debugging.

  * `--depth NUM`:
    Search up to NUM directories deep, -1 for unlimited. Default is 25.

  * `--[no]filename`:
    Print file names. Enabled by default, except when searching a single file.

  * `-f --[no]follow`:
    Follow symlinks. Default is false.

  * `-F --fixed-strings`:
    Alias for --literal for compatibility with grep.

  * `--[no]group`:
    The default, `--group`, lumps multiple matches in the same file
    together, and presents them under a single occurrence of the
    filename. `--nogroup` refrains from this, and instead places the
    filename at the start of each match line.

  * `-g PATTERN`:
    Print filenames matching PATTERN.

  * `-G --file-search-regex PATTERN`:
    Only search files whose names match PATTERN.

  * `-H --[no]heading`:
    Print filenames above matching contents.

  * `--hidden`:
    Search hidden files. This option obeys ignored files.

  * `--ignore PATTERN`:
    Ignore files/directories whose names match this pattern. Literal
    file and directory names are also allowed.

  * `--ignore-dir NAME`:
    Alias for --ignore for compatibility with ack.

  * `-i --ignore-case`:
    Match case-insensitively.

  * `-l --files-with-matches`:
    Only print the names of files containing matches, not the matching
    lines. An empty query will print all files that would be searched.

  * `-L --files-without-matches`:
    Only print the names of files that don't contain matches.

  * `--list-file-types`:
    See `FILE TYPES` below.

  * `-m --max-count NUM`:
    Skip the rest of a file after NUM matches. Default is 0, which never skips.

  * `--[no]mmap`:
    Toggle use of memory-mapped I/O. Defaults to true on platforms where
    `mmap()` is faster than `read()`. (All but macOS.)

  * `--[no]multiline`:
    Match regexes across newlines. Enabled by default.

  * `-n --norecurse`:
    Don't recurse into directories.

  * `--[no]numbers`:
    Print line numbers. Default is to omit line numbers when searching streams.

  * `-o --only-matching`:
    Print only the matching part of the lines.

  * `--one-device`:
    When recursing directories, don't scan dirs that reside on other storage
    devices. This lets you avoid scanning slow network mounts.
    This feature is not supported on all platforms.

  * `-p --path-to-ignore STRING`:
    Provide a path to a specific .ignore file.

  * `--pager COMMAND`:
    Use a pager such as `less`. Use `--nopager` to override. This option
    is also ignored if output is piped to another program.

  * `--parallel`:
    Parse the input stream as a search term, not data to search. This is meant
    to be used with tools such as GNU parallel. For example:
    `echo "foo\nbar\nbaz" | parallel "ag {} ."` will run 3 instances of ag,
    searching the current directory for "foo", "bar", and "baz".

  * `--print-long-lines`:
    Print matches on very long lines (> 2k characters by default).

  * `--passthrough --passthru`:
    When searching a stream, print all lines even if they don't match.

  * `-Q --literal`:
    Do not parse PATTERN as a regular expression. Try to match it literally.

  * `-r --recurse`:
    Recurse into directories when searching. Default is true.

  * `-s --case-sensitive`:
    Match case-sensitively.

  * `-S --smart-case`:
    Match case-sensitively if there are any uppercase letters in PATTERN,
    case-insensitively otherwise. Enabled by default.

  * `--search-binary`:
    Search binary files for matches.

  * `--silent`:
    Suppress all log messages, including errors.

  * `--stats`:
    Print stats (files scanned, time taken, etc).

  * `--stats-only`:
    Print stats (files scanned, time taken, etc) and nothing else.

  * `-t --all-text`:
    Search all text files. This doesn't include hidden files.

  * `-u --unrestricted`:
    Search *all* files. This ignores .ignore, .gitignore, etc. It searches
    binary and hidden files as well.

  * `-U --skip-vcs-ignores`:
    Ignore VCS ignore files (.gitignore, .hgignore), but still
    use .ignore.

  * `-v --invert-match`:
    Match every line *not* containing the specified pattern.

  * `-V --version`:
    Print version info.

  * `--vimgrep`:
    Output results in the same form as Vim's `:vimgrep /pattern/g`

    Here is a ~/.vimrc configuration example:

    `set grepprg=ag\ --vimgrep\ $*`
    `set grepformat=%f:%l:%c:%m`

    Then use `:grep` to grep for something.
    Then use `:copen`, `:cn`, `:cp`, etc. to navigate through the matches.

  * `-w --word-regexp`:
    Only match whole words.

  * `--workers NUM`:
    Use NUM worker threads. Default is the number of CPU cores, with a max of 8.

  * `-W --width NUM`:
    Truncate match lines after NUM characters.

  * `-z --search-zip`:
    Search contents of compressed files. Currently, gz and xz are supported.
    This option requires that ag is built with lzma and zlib.

  * `-0 --null --print0`:
    Separate the filenames with `\0`, rather than `\n`:
    this allows `xargs -0 <command>` to correctly process filenames containing
    spaces or newlines.


## FILE TYPES

It is possible to restrict the types of files searched. For example, passing
`--html` will search only files with the extensions `htm`, `html`, `shtml`
or `xhtml`. For a list of supported types, run `ag --list-file-types`.

## IGNORING FILES

By default, ag will ignore files whose names match patterns in .gitignore,
.hgignore, or .ignore. These files can be anywhere in the directories being
searched. Binary files are ignored by default as well. Finally, ag looks in
$HOME/.agignore for ignore patterns.

If you want to ignore .gitignore and .hgignore, but still take .ignore into
account, use `-U`.

Use the `-t` option to search all text files; `-a` to search all files; and `-u`
to search all, including hidden files.

## EXAMPLES

`ag printf`:
  Find matches for "printf" in the current directory.

`ag foo /bar/`:
  Find matches for "foo" in path /bar/.

`ag -- --foo`:
  Find matches for "--foo" in the current directory. (As with most UNIX command
  line utilities, "--" is used to signify that the remaining arguments should
  not be treated as options.)

## ABOUT

ag was originally created by Geoff Greer. More information (and the latest
release) can be found at http://geoff.greer.fm/ag

## SEE ALSO

def parse_filetypes(text):
    """Parse filetypes text block into dict: name -> list of suffixes."""
    result = {}
    name = None
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        line = raw.rstrip("\n")
        if line.startswith("  --"):
            name = line.strip()[2:]
            result[name] = []
        elif line.startswith("      ") and name is not None:
            exts = [e for e in line.strip().split("  ") if e]
            # Normalize: split on whitespace to handle single spaces
            final_exts = []
            for chunk in exts:
                for part in chunk.split():
                    if part.startswith("."):
                        final_exts.append(part)
                    elif part:
                        final_exts.append("." + part)
            result[name].extend(final_exts)
    return result

def file_matches_filetype(name, exts):
    """Return True if filename matches one of the type extensions.
    Some entries are filenames (e.g. .Makefiles -> match 'Makefiles' as name)."""
    for ext in exts:
        # e.g., '.Makefiles' or '.Rakefile' are filenames, not real extensions
        # Treat any ext without a lowercase letter before a capital letter
        # generically: also try matching the whole file name.
        if name.endswith(ext):

    return False

        elif name == "_stats_only":

                else:
                    err_invalid_short(c)
                j += 1
            i += 1
        else:
            if pattern is None:
                pattern = a
            else:
                paths.append(a)
            i += 1

    return opts, pattern, paths

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

DEFAULT_IGNORES = {
    # VCS dirs that are always ignored
    ".git", ".hg", ".svn", ".bzr", "CVS", "_darcs", ".bzrignore",
}

BINARY_EXTS = {
    ".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".gif", ".bmp", ".ico", ".tiff", ".tif",
    ".pdf", ".zip", ".tar", ".gz", ".bz2", ".xz", ".7z", ".rar",
    ".exe", ".dll", ".so", ".dylib", ".o", ".obj", ".a", ".lib",
    ".class", ".jar", ".pyc", ".pyo", ".wasm",
    ".mp3", ".mp4", ".avi", ".mov", ".mkv", ".wav", ".ogg", ".flac",
    ".bin", ".iso", ".dmg",
}


def gitignore_to_regex(pattern):
    """Convert a gitignore-style pattern to a regex function.
    Returns (regex, dir_only, negate)"""
    negate = False
    if pattern.startswith("!"):
        negate = True
        pattern = pattern[1:]
    dir_only = False
    if pattern.endswith("/"):
        dir_only = True
        pattern = pattern[:-1]
    anchored = False
    if pattern.startswith("/"):
        anchored = True
        pattern = pattern[1:]
    elif "/" in pattern[:-1]:
        anchored = True
    # Build a fnmatch-style regex
    # We'll convert glob to regex manually since '/' and '**' have special meaning
    rgx = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(pattern):
        c = pattern[i]
        if c == "*":
            if i + 1 < len(pattern) and pattern[i + 1] == "*":
                # **
                rgx.append(".*")
                i += 2
                if i < len(pattern) and pattern[i] == "/":
                    i += 1
            else:
                rgx.append("[^/]*")
                i += 1
        elif c == "?":
            rgx.append("[^/]")
            i += 1
        elif c == ".":
            rgx.append(r"\.")
            i += 1
        elif c in "()+|^$@{}\\":
            rgx.append("\\" + c)
            i += 1
        else:
            rgx.append(c)
            i += 1
    regex_str = "".join(rgx)
    if anchored:
        regex_str = "^" + regex_str + "$"
    else:
        regex_str = "(^|/)" + regex_str + "$"
    try:
        return re.compile(regex_str), dir_only, negate
    except re.error:
        return None, dir_only, negate


class IgnoreSet:
    def __init__(self):
        self.patterns = []  # list of (regex, dir_only, negate)

    def add_pattern(self, pat):
        pat = pat.strip()
        if not pat or pat.startswith("#"):
            return
        compiled = gitignore_to_regex(pat)
        if compiled[0] is not None:
            self.patterns.append(compiled)

    def add_patterns(self, patterns):
        for p in patterns:
            self.add_pattern(p)

    def matches(self, relpath, is_dir):
        """Check if relpath (posix separated, relative to this ignore's root)
        matches an ignore pattern."""
        matched = False
        for regex, dir_only, negate in self.patterns:
            if dir_only and not is_dir:
                continue
            if regex.search(relpath):
                matched = not negate
        return matched


def load_ignore_file(path):
    patterns = []
    try:
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
            for line in f:
                line = line.rstrip("\n").rstrip("\r")
                if line and not line.startswith("#"):
                    patterns.append(line)
    except (IOError, OSError):
        pass
    return patterns


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Regex building
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def build_regex(pattern, opts):
    flags = 0
    if opts.literal:
        pat = re.escape(pattern)
    else:
        pat = pattern
    if opts.word_regexp:
        pat = r"\b(?:" + pat + r")\b"
    # Smart case
    case_insensitive = False
    if opts.ignore_case:
        case_insensitive = True
    elif opts.case_sensitive:
        case_insensitive = False
    elif opts.smart_case:
        # case-insensitive unless pattern contains uppercase
        if not any(c.isupper() for c in pattern):
            case_insensitive = True
    if case_insensitive:
        flags |= re.IGNORECASE
    # Multiline by default? In ag, lines are matched one at a time in practice.
    try:
        return re.compile(pat, flags)
    except re.error as e:
        sys.stderr.write("%s: error: bad regex '%s': %s\n" % (sys.argv[0], pattern, e))
        sys.exit(2)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def is_binary_data(data):
    """Heuristic: file is binary if it contains a NUL byte in first 512 bytes."""
    head = data[:512]
    return b"\x00" in head

class SearchStats:
    def __init__(self):
        self.total_matches = 0
        self.files_with_matches = 0
        self.files_searched = 0
        self.bytes_searched = 0
        self.start_time = time.time()


class Output:
    def __init__(self, opts):
        self.opts = opts
        self.use_color = self._decide_color()
        self.stdout_is_tty = sys.stdout.isatty()
        self._first_file = True

    def _decide_color(self):
        if self.opts.color is False:
            return False
        if self.opts.color is True:
            return True
        return sys.stdout.isatty()

    def color_wrap(self, code, text):
        if not self.use_color:
            return text
        return "\033[" + code + "m" + text + "\033[0m\033[K"

    def write(self, s):
        try:
            sys.stdout.write(s)
        except BrokenPipeError:
            sys.exit(0)


def find_matches_in_line(line_text, regex):
    """Return list of (start, end) spans for all matches in a line."""
    result = []
    for m in regex.finditer(line_text):
        s, e = m.span()
        if s == e:
            # Zero-width match; advance by 1 to avoid infinite loop
            continue
        result.append((s, e))
    return result


def read_file_bytes(path):
    try:
        with open(path, "rb") as f:
            return f.read()
    except (IOError, OSError) as e:
        return None


def split_lines_bytes(data):
    """Split bytes into lines. Returns list of bytes (without trailing newline)."""
    if not data:
        return []
    # Normalize CRLF -> LF for matching purposes
    if data.endswith(b"\n"):
        data_s = data[:-1]
    else:
        data_s = data
    return data_s.split(b"\n")


def decode_line(line_bytes):
    try:
        return line_bytes.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        return line_bytes.decode("latin-1", errors="replace")


def search_in_data(data, regex, opts, display_path, output, stats):
    """Search binary data for regex, print results. Returns match count."""
    lines = split_lines_bytes(data)
    line_matches = []  # list of (lineno, line_text, [(s,e)])
    for idx, lb in enumerate(lines, start=1):
        text = decode_line(lb)
        spans = find_matches_in_line(text, regex)
        is_match = bool(spans)
        if opts.invert_match:
            is_match = not is_match
            if is_match:
                spans = []
        if is_match:
            line_matches.append((idx, text, spans))

    if opts.max_count and len(line_matches) > opts.max_count:
        # Note: original counts by match count not line count; we approximate
        if not opts.silent:
            sys.stderr.write("ERR: Too many matches in %s. Skipping the rest of this file.\n" % display_path)
        line_matches = line_matches[:opts.max_count]

    if opts.files_with_matches:
        if line_matches:
            stats.files_with_matches += 1
            if opts.print0:
                output.write(display_path + "\x00")
            else:
                output.write(display_path + "\n")
        return len(line_matches)

    if opts.files_without_matches:
        if not line_matches:
            if opts.print0:
                output.write(display_path + "\x00")
            else:
                output.write(display_path + "\n")
        return len(line_matches)

    if opts.count:
        total = sum(len(m[2]) if m[2] else 1 for m in line_matches)
        if line_matches:
            stats.files_with_matches += 1
        if output.opts.show_filename():
            output.write("%s:%d\n" % (display_path, total))
        else:
            output.write("%d\n" % total)
        return total

    if not line_matches:
        if opts.print_all_files:
            if output.opts.heading is not False:
                output.write(output.color_wrap(opts.color_path, display_path) + "\n")
        return 0

    stats.files_with_matches += 1

    # Decide heading/break defaults
    heading = opts.heading
    brk = opts.break_between
    if heading is None:
        heading = True
    if brk is None:
        brk = True

    show_filename = output.opts.show_filename()
    show_numbers = opts.numbers
    if show_numbers is None:
        show_numbers = True

    # Output
    if heading and show_filename:
        if not output._first_file and brk:
            output.write("\n")
        output.write(output.color_wrap(opts.color_path, display_path) + "\n")
    output._first_file = False

    before_n = opts.before
    after_n = opts.after

    # Build a set of matched line numbers for context
    matched_set = set(lm[0] for lm in line_matches)
    # Build "display" set including context lines
    display_lines = set()
    for ln in matched_set:
        for off in range(-before_n, after_n + 1):
            dl = ln + off
            if 1 <= dl <= len(lines):
                display_lines.add(dl)
    sorted_display = sorted(display_lines)

    # Build line text cache (decoded)
    def line_text_at(i):
        if 1 <= i <= len(lines):
            return decode_line(lines[i - 1])
        return ""

    total_match_count = 0
    prev_line = None
    for ln in sorted_display:
        if prev_line is not None and ln != prev_line + 1:
            output.write("--\n")
        prev_line = ln
        text = line_text_at(ln)
        is_match_line = ln in matched_set
        spans = []
        if is_match_line:
            # Get spans from line_matches
            for lm in line_matches:
                if lm[0] == ln:
                    spans = lm[2]
                    break
            total_match_count += len(spans) if spans else 1

        # Determine separators
        sep = ":" if is_match_line else "-"
        parts = []
        if not heading and show_filename:
            parts.append(output.color_wrap(opts.color_path, display_path))
            parts.append(sep)
        if show_numbers:
            parts.append(output.color_wrap(opts.color_line, str(ln)))
            parts.append(sep)
        if opts.column and is_match_line and spans:
            col = spans[0][0] + 1
            parts.append(output.color_wrap(opts.color_line, str(col)))
            parts.append(sep)

        prefix = "".join(parts)

        if opts.only_matching and is_match_line:
            for s, e in spans:
                output.write(prefix + output.color_wrap(opts.color_match, text[s:e]) + "\n")
        else:
            if is_match_line and spans:
                rendered = render_line_with_matches(text, spans, opts, output)
            else:
                rendered = text
            if opts.width and len(rendered) > opts.width:
                # Naive truncation - note: ignores color escapes
                pass
            output.write(prefix + rendered + "\n")

    return total_match_count


def render_line_with_matches(text, spans, opts, output):
    out = []
    prev = 0
    for s, e in spans:
        out.append(text[prev:s])
        out.append(output.color_wrap(opts.color_match, text[s:e]))
        prev = e
    out.append(text[prev:])
    return "".join(out)


def search_binary_file(display_path, output, stats):
    """Print the 'Binary file X matches.' message."""
    output.write("Binary file %s matches.\n" % display_path)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# File walking
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def should_search_file_by_type(name, opts):
    if not opts.file_type_filters:
        return True
    for exts in opts.file_type_filters:
        if file_matches_filetype(name, exts):
            return True
    return False


def filename_is_ignored(name, path, is_dir, opts, ignore_stack):
    """Check ignore rules. ignore_stack is a list of (root_path, IgnoreSet)."""
    if opts.unrestricted:
        return False
    # Hidden
    if not opts.hidden and not opts.unrestricted and name.startswith("."):
        # .git etc; also the user may want to keep some
        return True
    # VCS dirs
    if is_dir and name in DEFAULT_IGNORES and not opts.unrestricted:
        return True
    # Per --ignore patterns
    for pat in opts.ignore_patterns:
        if fnmatch.fnmatchcase(name, pat):
            return True
        if name == pat:
            return True
    # gitignore/ignore stack
    for root, ig_set in ignore_stack:
        try:
            rel = os.path.relpath(path, root)
        except ValueError:
            continue
        rel = rel.replace(os.sep, "/")
        if ig_set.matches(rel, is_dir):
            return True
        if ig_set.matches(name, is_dir):
            return True
    return False


def walk_paths(paths, opts):
    """Yield (display_path, real_path) for each file to search."""
    # Build per-path traversal.
    # Initial ignore stack: process --path-to-ignore files and home agignore
    base_ignores = IgnoreSet()
    home = os.environ.get("HOME", "")
    if home:
        ag_ignore = os.path.join(home, ".agignore")
        if os.path.exists(ag_ignore):
            base_ignores.add_patterns(load_ignore_file(ag_ignore))
    for p in opts.path_to_ignore:
        base_ignores.add_patterns(load_ignore_file(p))

    for path in paths:
        if os.path.isfile(path):
            yield path, path
            continue
        if not os.path.isdir(path):
            if not opts.silent:
                sys.stderr.write("ERR: Error stat()ing: %s\n" % path)
                sys.stderr.write("ERR: Error opening directory %s: %s\n" %
                                 (path, os.strerror(errno.ENOENT)))
            continue

        yield from walk_dir(path, opts, base_ignores)


def walk_dir(root, opts, base_ignores):
    """Generator that yields files under root."""
    show_prefix = root
    # If path was given as "." or doesn't end with /, we still show "./" prefix
    # ag uses "./" for implicit root, and full path if explicit.

    # Actually ag uses the path as given, so "." becomes "./file", "/abs" becomes "/abs/file"
    prefix = root if root.endswith(os.sep) else root + os.sep
    # Special case for "."
    # Leave as-is; os.path.join will handle

    ignore_stack = [(root, _clone_base(base_ignores))]
    # Load initial ignores at root
    _append_dir_ignores(root, ignore_stack[0][1], opts)

    yield from _walk_recurse(root, root, prefix, opts, ignore_stack, depth=0)


def _clone_base(ig):
    out = IgnoreSet()
    out.patterns = list(ig.patterns)
    return out


def _append_dir_ignores(directory, ig_set, opts):
    """Scan directory for .ignore/.gitignore/.hgignore and add to ig_set."""
    if opts.unrestricted:
        return
    for fname in (".ignore",):
        p = os.path.join(directory, fname)
        if os.path.isfile(p):
            ig_set.add_patterns(load_ignore_file(p))
    if not opts.skip_vcs_ignores:
        for fname in (".gitignore", ".hgignore"):
            p = os.path.join(directory, fname)
            if os.path.isfile(p):
                ig_set.add_patterns(load_ignore_file(p))


def _walk_recurse(current_dir, display_base, display_prefix, opts,
                  ignore_stack, depth):
    if opts.depth >= 0 and depth > opts.depth:
        return
    try:
        entries = sorted(os.listdir(current_dir))
    except (IOError, OSError) as e:
        if not opts.silent:
            sys.stderr.write("ERR: Error opening directory %s: %s\n" %
                             (current_dir, e.strerror or str(e)))
        return

    # First-level dir: ignore stack already set up
    # For subdir ignores, we push a new one
    sub_ignore = _clone_base(ignore_stack[-1][1])
    _append_dir_ignores(current_dir, sub_ignore, opts)
    local_stack = ignore_stack[:-1] + [(ignore_stack[-1][0], sub_ignore)]

    for name in entries:
        full = os.path.join(current_dir, name)
        try:
            st = os.lstat(full)
        except (IOError, OSError):
            continue
        is_link = stat.S_ISLNK(st.st_mode)
        if is_link and not opts.follow_symlinks:
            continue
        try:
            st_real = os.stat(full)
        except (IOError, OSError):
            continue
        is_dir = stat.S_ISDIR(st_real.st_mode)

        if filename_is_ignored(name, full, is_dir, opts, local_stack):
            continue

        if is_dir:
            if not opts.recurse:
                continue
            yield from _walk_recurse(full, display_base,
                                     display_prefix, opts, local_stack,
                                     depth=depth + 1)
        elif stat.S_ISREG(st_real.st_mode):
            # Build display path: use same relative form as ag
            # ag usually shows paths as given. When root is ".", it prefixes "./"
            rel = os.path.relpath(full, display_base)
            if display_base == ".":
                display = rel
            else:
                # Use prefix path as given
                display = os.path.join(display_base, rel)
                # Normalize if the prefix is absolute or relative
            # Match ag's typical format: if root was ".", use "./X"
            # Actually ag strips "./" typically for the current dir.
            yield display, full

# Main
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def main():
    opts, pattern, paths = parse_args(sys.argv)

    stdin_is_tty = sys.stdin.isatty()
    stdout_is_tty = sys.stdout.isatty()

    # Decide whether to search stdin
    # If no paths provided AND stdin is not a tty, search stdin
    if opts.parallel:
        # special handling not implemented
        pass

    if opts.filename_pattern_print is not None and pattern is None:
        # -g mode: pattern is the -g arg itself
        pattern = opts.filename_pattern_print

    if pattern is None:
        # Print usage; ag does this
        sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXT)
        sys.exit(1)

    if pattern == "":
        sys.stderr.write("ERR: Error: No query. What do you want to search for?\n")
        sys.exit(1)

    # -g mode: print matching filenames
    if opts.filename_pattern_print is not None:
        rgx = build_regex(opts.filename_pattern_print, opts)
        walk_src = paths if paths else ["."]
        any_match = False
        if paths or not stdin_is_tty:
            for display, real in walk_paths(walk_src, opts):
                name = os.path.basename(display)
                if rgx.search(name) or rgx.search(display):
                    # Strip leading ./ if rooted at '.'
                    pretty = display
                    if pretty.startswith("./"):
                        pretty = pretty[2:]
                    sys.stdout.write(pretty + "\n")
                    any_match = True
        sys.exit(0 if any_match else 1)

    regex = build_regex(pattern, opts)
    stats = SearchStats()
    output = Output(opts)

    # stdin mode
    if not paths and not stdin_is_tty:
        data = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
        opts.print_filename = False if opts.print_filename is None else opts.print_filename
        # Numbers default off for streams
        if opts.numbers is None:
            opts.numbers = False
        if opts.passthrough and not opts.invert_match:
            # print all lines, highlighting matches
            text = data.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
            # We need to output line by line
            lines = text.split("\n")
            if text.endswith("\n"):
                lines = lines[:-1]
            for line in lines:
                spans = find_matches_in_line(line, regex)
                if spans:
                    sys.stdout.write(render_line_with_matches(line, spans, opts, output) + "\n")
                    stats.total_matches += len(spans)
                else:
                    sys.stdout.write(line + "\n")
            sys.exit(0 if stats.total_matches > 0 else 1)
        display_name = "-"
        # For stdin, ag doesn't print a filename
        total = search_in_data(data, regex, opts, display_name, output, stats)
        stats.total_matches += total
        sys.exit(0 if stats.total_matches > 0 else 1)

    if not paths:
        paths = ["."]

    # Single-file mode: don't print filename unless user asked
    if len(paths) == 1 and os.path.isfile(paths[0]):
        if opts.print_filename is None:
            opts.print_filename = False
            opts.heading = False if opts.heading is None else opts.heading

    # Default heading based on multiple files
    # ag prints headings by default for multi-file
    # (opts.heading is None means auto => True for files)

    any_matches = False

    for display, real in walk_paths(paths, opts):
        try:
            with open(real, "rb") as f:
                data = f.read()
        except (IOError, OSError) as e:
            if not opts.silent:
                sys.stderr.write("ERR: Error reading %s: %s\n" % (display, e))
            continue

        stats.files_searched += 1
        stats.bytes_searched += len(data)

        # Skip long-line files if --print-long-lines not set?
        # Heuristic: check for binary
        is_bin = is_binary_data(data)
        if is_bin and not opts.search_binary and not opts.unrestricted:
            # Check if any match
            if regex.search(data.decode("latin-1", errors="replace")):
                if not opts.files_with_matches and not opts.files_without_matches \
                        and not opts.count:
                    output.write("Binary file %s matches.\n" % display)
                    any_matches = True
                elif opts.files_with_matches:
                    if opts.print0:
                        output.write(display + "\x00")
                    else:
                        output.write(display + "\n")
                    any_matches = True
                    stats.files_with_matches += 1
            continue

        matches = search_in_data(data, regex, opts, display, output, stats)
        stats.total_matches += matches
        if matches:
            any_matches = True

    if opts.stats_only:
        print_stats(stats)
        sys.exit(0 if any_matches else 1)
    if opts.stats:
        print_stats(stats)

    sys.exit(0 if any_matches else 1)


def print_stats(stats):
    elapsed = time.time() - stats.start_time
    sys.stdout.write("%d matches\n" % stats.total_matches)
    sys.stdout.write("%d files contained matches\n" % stats.files_with_matches)
    sys.stdout.write("%d files searched\n" % stats.files_searched)
    sys.stdout.write("%d bytes searched\n" % stats.bytes_searched)
    sys.stdout.write("%f seconds\n" % elapsed)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        main()
    except BrokenPipeError:
        sys.exit(0)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        sys.exit(130)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""ag (The Silver Searcher) - reimplementation in Python."""

import errno
import fnmatch
import os
import re

import sys

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Embedded data - populated by compile.sh
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
VERSION_TEXT = r"""__VERSION_TEXT__"""
HELP_TEXT = r"""__HELP_TEXT__"""
FILETYPES_TEXT = r"""__FILETYPES_TEXT__"""

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers

PROG_NAME = "ag"  # match what the binary emits for err messages, kept simple


def parse_filetypes(text):
    """Parse filetypes text block into dict: name -> list of suffixes."""
    result = {}
    name = None
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        line = raw.rstrip("\n")
        if line.startswith("  --"):
            name = line.strip()[2:]
            result[name] = []
        elif line.startswith("      ") and name is not None:
            exts = [e for e in line.strip().split("  ") if e]
            # Normalize: split on whitespace to handle single spaces
            final_exts = []
            for chunk in exts:
                for part in chunk.split():
                    if part.startswith("."):
                        final_exts.append(part)
                    elif part:
                        final_exts.append("." + part)
            result[name].extend(final_exts)
    return result


FILETYPES = parse_filetypes(FILETYPES_TEXT)


def file_matches_filetype(name, exts):
    """Return True if filename matches one of the type extensions.
    Some entries are filenames (e.g. .Makefiles -> match 'Makefiles' as name)."""
    for ext in exts:
        # e.g., '.Makefiles' or '.Rakefile' are filenames, not real extensions
        # Treat any ext without a lowercase letter before a capital letter
        # generically: also try matching the whole file name.
        if name.endswith(ext):
            return True
        # Some 'extensions' in FILETYPES are actually basenames
        if name == ext.lstrip("."):
            return True

def parse_args(argv):
    opts = Options()
    pattern = None
    paths = []
    i = 1

    def set_flag(attr, val):
        if attr.startswith("_"):
            return  # silently accept ignored flags
        setattr(opts, attr, val)

    def do_method(name, arg=None):
        if name == "_group_on":
            opts.heading = True
            opts.break_between = True
        elif name == "_group_off":
            opts.heading = False
            opts.break_between = False
        elif name == "_smart_case":
            opts.smart_case = True
            opts.ignore_case = False
            opts.case_sensitive = False
        elif name == "_case_sensitive":
            opts.case_sensitive = True
            opts.smart_case = False
            opts.ignore_case = False
        elif name == "_stats_only":
            opts.stats = True
            opts.stats_only = True
        elif name == "_vimgrep":
            opts.vimgrep = True
            opts.heading = False
            opts.break_between = False
            opts.column = True
            opts.numbers = True
            opts.print_filename = True
        elif name == "_version":
            sys.stdout.write(VERSION_TEXT)
            sys.exit(0)
        elif name == "_help":
            sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXT)
            sys.exit(0)
        elif name == "_list_file_types":
            sys.stdout.write(FILETYPES_TEXT)
            sys.exit(0)

    while i < len(argv):
        a = argv[i]
        if a == "--":
            i += 1
            while i < len(argv):
                if pattern is None:
                    pattern = argv[i]
                else:
                    paths.append(argv[i])
                i += 1
            break
        if a.startswith("--"):
            eq_idx = a.find("=")
            if eq_idx >= 0:
                name = a[2:eq_idx]
                val = a[eq_idx + 1:]
                has_eqval = True
            else:
                name = a[2:]
                val = None
                has_eqval = False

            # Filetype flag?
            if name in FILETYPES:
                opts.file_type_filters.append(FILETYPES[name])
                i += 1
                continue

            if name not in LONG_OPTIONS:
                err_unrecognized_long(name)

            kind_tuple = LONG_OPTIONS[name]
            kind = kind_tuple[0]
            if kind == "flag":
                attr = kind_tuple[1]
                newval = kind_tuple[2]
                set_flag(attr, newval)
                i += 1
            elif kind == "method":
                mname = kind_tuple[1]
                do_method(mname)
                i += 1
            elif kind == "intopt":
                attr = kind_tuple[1]
                default = kind_tuple[2]
                if has_eqval:
                    try:
                        iv = int(val)
                    except ValueError:
                        err_requires_arg_long(name)
                    if attr == "context":
                        opts.before = iv
                        opts.after = iv
                    else:
                        setattr(opts, attr, iv)
                    i += 1
                else:
                    # next arg if numeric, else use default
                    nxt = argv[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(argv) else None
                    if nxt is not None and nxt.isdigit():
                        iv = int(nxt)
                        if attr == "context":
                            opts.before = iv
                            opts.after = iv
                        else:
                            setattr(opts, attr, iv)
                        i += 2
                    else:
                        iv = default
                        if attr == "context":
                            opts.before = iv
                            opts.after = iv
                        else:
                            setattr(opts, attr, iv)
                        i += 1
            elif kind == "strarg":
                attr = kind_tuple[1]
                if has_eqval:
                    v = val
                    i += 1
                else:
                    if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                        err_requires_arg_long(name)
                    v = argv[i + 1]
                    i += 2
                if attr == "ignore_patterns":
                    opts.ignore_patterns.append(v)
                elif attr == "path_to_ignore":
                    opts.path_to_ignore.append(v)
                elif attr == "depth":
                    try:
                        opts.depth = int(v)
                    except ValueError:
                        err_requires_arg_long(name)
                elif attr == "max_count":
                    try:
                        opts.max_count = int(v)
                    except ValueError:
                        err_requires_arg_long(name)
                elif attr == "width":
                    try:
                        opts.width = int(v)
                    except ValueError:
                        err_requires_arg_long(name)
                elif attr.startswith("_"):
                    pass
                else:
                    setattr(opts, attr, v)
        elif a.startswith("-") and len(a) > 1 and a != "-":
            # Short option cluster
            j = 1
            while j < len(a):
                c = a[j]
                consumed_arg = None
                if c in "ABCmWGgp":
                    # options that need arg (either rest of cluster or next argv)
                    if j + 1 < len(a):
                        consumed_arg = a[j + 1:]
                        j = len(a)
                    else:
                        if i + 1 < len(argv):
                            consumed_arg = argv[i + 1]
                            i += 1
                            j = len(a)
                        else:
                            # Some options accept optional numeric args
                            if c in "ABC":
                                consumed_arg = None
                                j = len(a)
                            else:
                                err_requires_arg_short(c)

                if c == "a":
                    opts.all_types = True
                elif c == "A":
                    if consumed_arg is None:
                        opts.after = 2
                    else:
                        try:
                            opts.after = int(consumed_arg)
                        except ValueError:
                            err_requires_arg_short(c)
                elif c == "B":
                    if consumed_arg is None:
                        opts.before = 2
                    else:
                        try:
                            opts.before = int(consumed_arg)
                        except ValueError:
                            err_requires_arg_short(c)
                elif c == "C":
                    if consumed_arg is None:
                        opts.before = 2
                        opts.after = 2
                    else:
                        try:
                            n = int(consumed_arg)
                            opts.before = n
                            opts.after = n
                        except ValueError:
                            err_requires_arg_short(c)
                elif c == "c":
                    opts.count = True
                elif c == "D":
                    opts.debug = True
                elif c == "f":
                    opts.follow_symlinks = True
                elif c == "F":
                    opts.literal = True
                elif c == "G":
                    opts.file_search_regex = consumed_arg
                elif c == "g":
                    opts.filename_pattern_print = consumed_arg
                elif c == "H":
                    opts.heading = True
                elif c == "h":
                    sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXT)
                    sys.exit(0)
                elif c == "i":
                    opts.ignore_case = True
                    opts.smart_case = False
                elif c == "L":
                    opts.files_without_matches = True
                elif c == "l":
                    opts.files_with_matches = True
                elif c == "m":
                    try:
                        opts.max_count = int(consumed_arg)
                    except (ValueError, TypeError):
                        err_requires_arg_short(c)
                elif c == "n":
                    opts.recurse = False
                elif c == "o":
                    opts.only_matching = True
                elif c == "p":
                    opts.path_to_ignore.append(consumed_arg)
                elif c == "Q":
                    opts.literal = True
                elif c == "r":
                    opts.recurse = True
                elif c == "s":
                    opts.case_sensitive = True
                    opts.smart_case = False
                    opts.ignore_case = False
                elif c == "S":
                    opts.smart_case = True
                    opts.case_sensitive = False
                    opts.ignore_case = False
                elif c == "t":
                    opts.all_text = True
                elif c == "u":
                    opts.unrestricted = True
                elif c == "U":
                    opts.skip_vcs_ignores = True
                elif c == "v":
                    opts.invert_match = True
                elif c == "V":
                    sys.stdout.write(VERSION_TEXT)
                    sys.exit(0)
                elif c == "w":
                    opts.word_regexp = True
                elif c == "W":
                    try:
                        opts.width = int(consumed_arg)
                    except (ValueError, TypeError):
                        err_requires_arg_short(c)
                elif c == "z":
                    opts.search_zip = True
                elif c == "0":
                    opts.print0 = True
                elif c == "?":
                    sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXT)
                    sys.exit(0)
                else:
                    err_invalid_short(c)
                j += 1
            i += 1
        else:
            if pattern is None:
                pattern = a
            else:
                paths.append(a)
            i += 1

    return opts, pattern, paths

def gitignore_to_regex(pattern):
    """Convert a gitignore-style pattern to a regex function.
    Returns (regex, dir_only, negate)"""
    negate = False
    if pattern.startswith("!"):
        negate = True
        pattern = pattern[1:]
    dir_only = False
    if pattern.endswith("/"):
        dir_only = True
        pattern = pattern[:-1]
    anchored = False
    if pattern.startswith("/"):
        anchored = True
        pattern = pattern[1:]
    elif "/" in pattern[:-1]:
        anchored = True
    # Build a fnmatch-style regex
    # We'll convert glob to regex manually since '/' and '**' have special meaning
    rgx = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(pattern):
        c = pattern[i]
        if c == "*":
            if i + 1 < len(pattern) and pattern[i + 1] == "*":
                # **
                rgx.append(".*")
                i += 2
                if i < len(pattern) and pattern[i] == "/":
                    i += 1
            else:
                rgx.append("[^/]*")
                i += 1
        elif c == "?":
            rgx.append("[^/]")
            i += 1
        elif c == ".":
            rgx.append(r"\.")
            i += 1
        elif c in "()+|^$@{}\\":
            rgx.append("\\" + c)
            i += 1
        else:
            rgx.append(c)
            i += 1
    regex_str = "".join(rgx)
    if anchored:
        regex_str = "^" + regex_str + "$"
    else:
        regex_str = "(^|/)" + regex_str + "$"
    try:
        return re.compile(regex_str), dir_only, negate
    except re.error:
        return None, dir_only, negate


class IgnoreSet:
    def __init__(self):
        self.patterns = []  # list of (regex, dir_only, negate)

    def add_pattern(self, pat):
        pat = pat.strip()
        if not pat or pat.startswith("#"):
            return
        compiled = gitignore_to_regex(pat)
        if compiled[0] is not None:
            self.patterns.append(compiled)

    def add_patterns(self, patterns):
        for p in patterns:
            self.add_pattern(p)

    def matches(self, relpath, is_dir):
        """Check if relpath (posix separated, relative to this ignore's root)
        matches an ignore pattern."""
        matched = False
        for regex, dir_only, negate in self.patterns:
            if dir_only and not is_dir:
                continue
            if regex.search(relpath):
                matched = not negate
        return matched


def load_ignore_file(path):
    patterns = []
    try:
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
            for line in f:
                line = line.rstrip("\n").rstrip("\r")
                if line and not line.startswith("#"):
                    patterns.append(line)
    except (IOError, OSError):
        pass
    return patterns


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Regex building
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def build_regex(pattern, opts):
    flags = 0
    if opts.literal:
        pat = re.escape(pattern)
    else:
        pat = pattern
    if opts.word_regexp:
        pat = r"\b(?:" + pat + r")\b"
    # Smart case
    case_insensitive = False
    if opts.ignore_case:
        case_insensitive = True
    elif opts.case_sensitive:
        case_insensitive = False
    elif opts.smart_case:
        # case-insensitive unless pattern contains uppercase
        if not any(c.isupper() for c in pattern):
            case_insensitive = True
    if case_insensitive:
        flags |= re.IGNORECASE
    # Multiline by default? In ag, lines are matched one at a time in practice.
    try:
        return re.compile(pat, flags)
    except re.error as e:
        sys.stderr.write("%s: error: bad regex '%s': %s\n" % (sys.argv[0], pattern, e))
        sys.exit(2)

def is_binary_data(data):
    """Heuristic: file is binary if it contains a NUL byte in first 512 bytes."""
    head = data[:512]
    return b"\x00" in head

class SearchStats:
    def __init__(self):
        self.total_matches = 0
        self.files_with_matches = 0
        self.files_searched = 0
        self.bytes_searched = 0
        self.start_time = time.time()


class Output:
    def __init__(self, opts):
        self.opts = opts
        self.use_color = self._decide_color()
        self.stdout_is_tty = sys.stdout.isatty()
        self._first_file = True

    def _decide_color(self):
        if self.opts.color is False:
            return False
        if self.opts.color is True:
            return True
        return sys.stdout.isatty()

    def color_wrap(self, code, text):
        if not self.use_color:
            return text
        return "\033[" + code + "m" + text + "\033[0m\033[K"

    def write(self, s):
        try:
            sys.stdout.write(s)
        except BrokenPipeError:
            sys.exit(0)


def find_matches_in_line(line_text, regex):
    """Return list of (start, end) spans for all matches in a line."""
    result = []
    for m in regex.finditer(line_text):
        s, e = m.span()
        if s == e:
            # Zero-width match; advance by 1 to avoid infinite loop
            continue
        result.append((s, e))
    return result


def read_file_bytes(path):
    try:
        with open(path, "rb") as f:
            return f.read()
    except (IOError, OSError) as e:
        return None


def split_lines_bytes(data):
    """Split bytes into lines. Returns list of bytes (without trailing newline)."""
    if not data:
        return []
    # Normalize CRLF -> LF for matching purposes
    if data.endswith(b"\n"):
        data_s = data[:-1]
    else:
        data_s = data
    return data_s.split(b"\n")


def decode_line(line_bytes):
    try:
        return line_bytes.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        return line_bytes.decode("latin-1", errors="replace")


def search_in_data(data, regex, opts, display_path, output, stats):
    """Search binary data for regex, print results. Returns match count."""
    lines = split_lines_bytes(data)
    line_matches = []  # list of (lineno, line_text, [(s,e)])
    for idx, lb in enumerate(lines, start=1):
        text = decode_line(lb)
        spans = find_matches_in_line(text, regex)
        is_match = bool(spans)
        if opts.invert_match:
            is_match = not is_match
            if is_match:
                spans = []
        if is_match:
            line_matches.append((idx, text, spans))

    if opts.max_count and len(line_matches) > opts.max_count:
        # Note: original counts by match count not line count; we approximate
        if not opts.silent:
            sys.stderr.write("ERR: Too many matches in %s. Skipping the rest of this file.\n" % display_path)
        line_matches = line_matches[:opts.max_count]

    if opts.files_with_matches:
        if line_matches:
            stats.files_with_matches += 1
            if opts.print0:
                output.write(display_path + "\x00")
            else:
                output.write(display_path + "\n")
        return len(line_matches)

    if opts.files_without_matches:
        if not line_matches:
            if opts.print0:
                output.write(display_path + "\x00")
            else:
                output.write(display_path + "\n")
        return len(line_matches)

    if opts.count:
        total = sum(len(m[2]) if m[2] else 1 for m in line_matches)
        if line_matches:
            stats.files_with_matches += 1
        if output.opts.show_filename():
            output.write("%s:%d\n" % (display_path, total))
        else:
            output.write("%d\n" % total)
        return total

    if not line_matches:
        if opts.print_all_files:
            if output.opts.heading is not False:
                output.write(output.color_wrap(opts.color_path, display_path) + "\n")
        return 0

    stats.files_with_matches += 1

    # Decide heading/break defaults
    heading = opts.heading
    brk = opts.break_between
    if heading is None:
        heading = True
    if brk is None:
        brk = True

    show_filename = output.opts.show_filename()
    show_numbers = opts.numbers
    if show_numbers is None:
        show_numbers = True

    # Output
    if heading and show_filename:
        if not output._first_file and brk:
            output.write("\n")
        output.write(output.color_wrap(opts.color_path, display_path) + "\n")
    output._first_file = False

    before_n = opts.before
    after_n = opts.after

    # Build a set of matched line numbers for context
    matched_set = set(lm[0] for lm in line_matches)
    # Build "display" set including context lines
    display_lines = set()
    for ln in matched_set:
        for off in range(-before_n, after_n + 1):
            dl = ln + off
            if 1 <= dl <= len(lines):
                display_lines.add(dl)
    sorted_display = sorted(display_lines)

    # Build line text cache (decoded)
    def line_text_at(i):
        if 1 <= i <= len(lines):
            return decode_line(lines[i - 1])
        return ""

    if not opts.hidden and not opts.unrestricted and name.startswith("."):

    out = IgnoreSet()
    out.patterns = list(ig.patterns)
    return out

    """Scan directory for .ignore/.gitignore/.hgignore and add to ig_set."""
    if opts.unrestricted:
        return
    for fname in (".ignore",):
        p = os.path.join(directory, fname)
        if os.path.isfile(p):
            ig_set.add_patterns(load_ignore_file(p))
    if not opts.skip_vcs_ignores:
        for fname in (".gitignore", ".hgignore"):
            p = os.path.join(directory, fname)
            if os.path.isfile(p):

def _walk_recurse(current_dir, display_base, display_prefix, opts,
                  ignore_stack, depth):
    if opts.depth >= 0 and depth > opts.depth:
        return
    try:
        entries = sorted(os.listdir(current_dir))
    except (IOError, OSError) as e:
        if not opts.silent:
            sys.stderr.write("ERR: Error opening directory %s: %s\n" %
                             (current_dir, e.strerror or str(e)))
        return

    # First-level dir: ignore stack already set up
    # For subdir ignores, we push a new one
    sub_ignore = _clone_base(ignore_stack[-1][1])
    _append_dir_ignores(current_dir, sub_ignore, opts)
    local_stack = ignore_stack[:-1] + [(ignore_stack[-1][0], sub_ignore)]

    for name in entries:
        full = os.path.join(current_dir, name)
        try:
            st = os.lstat(full)
        except (IOError, OSError):

        is_link = stat.S_ISLNK(st.st_mode)
        if is_link and not opts.follow_symlinks:

        except (IOError, OSError):

        is_dir = stat.S_ISDIR(st_real.st_mode)

        if filename_is_ignored(name, full, is_dir, opts, local_stack):

                                     display_prefix, opts, local_stack,
                                     depth=depth + 1)

            # ag usually shows paths as given. When root is ".", it prefixes "./"

            # Match ag's typical format: if root was ".", use "./X"
            # Actually ag strips "./" typically for the current dir.
            yield display, full

                        i += 2
                    else:
                        iv = default
                        if attr == "context":
                            opts.before = iv
                            opts.after = iv
                        else:
                            setattr(opts, attr, iv)
                        i += 1
            elif kind == "strarg":
                attr = kind_tuple[1]
                if has_eqval:
                    v = val
                    i += 1
                else:
                    if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                        err_requires_arg_long(name)
                    v = argv[i + 1]
                    i += 2
                if attr == "ignore_patterns":
                    opts.ignore_patterns.append(v)
                elif attr == "path_to_ignore":
                    opts.path_to_ignore.append(v)
                elif attr == "depth":
                    try:
                        opts.depth = int(v)
                    except ValueError:
                        err_requires_arg_long(name)
                elif attr == "max_count":
                    try:
                        opts.max_count = int(v)
                    except ValueError:
                        err_requires_arg_long(name)
                elif attr == "width":
                    try:
                        opts.width = int(v)
                    except ValueError:
                        err_requires_arg_long(name)
                elif attr.startswith("_"):
                    pass
                else:
                    setattr(opts, attr, v)
        elif a.startswith("-") and len(a) > 1 and a != "-":
            # Short option cluster
            j = 1
            while j < len(a):
                c = a[j]
                consumed_arg = None
                if c in "ABCmWGgp":
                    # options that need arg (either rest of cluster or next argv)
                    if j + 1 < len(a):
                        consumed_arg = a[j + 1:]
                        j = len(a)
                    else:
                        if i + 1 < len(argv):
                            consumed_arg = argv[i + 1]
                            i += 1
                            j = len(a)
                        else:
                            # Some options accept optional numeric args
                            if c in "ABC":
                                consumed_arg = None
                                j = len(a)
                            else:
                                err_requires_arg_short(c)

                if c == "a":
                    opts.all_types = True
                elif c == "A":
                    if consumed_arg is None:
                        opts.after = 2
                    else:
                        try:
                            opts.after = int(consumed_arg)
                        except ValueError:
                            err_requires_arg_short(c)
                elif c == "B":
                    if consumed_arg is None:
                        opts.before = 2
                    else:
                        try:
                            opts.before = int(consumed_arg)
                        except ValueError:
                            err_requires_arg_short(c)
                elif c == "C":
                    if consumed_arg is None:
                        opts.before = 2
                        opts.after = 2
                    else:
                        try:
                            n = int(consumed_arg)
                            opts.before = n
                            opts.after = n
                        except ValueError:
                            err_requires_arg_short(c)
                elif c == "c":
                    opts.count = True
                elif c == "D":
                    opts.debug = True
                elif c == "f":
                    opts.follow_symlinks = True
                elif c == "F":
                    opts.literal = True
                elif c == "G":
                    opts.file_search_regex = consumed_arg
                elif c == "g":
                    opts.filename_pattern_print = consumed_arg
                elif c == "H":
                    opts.heading = True
                elif c == "h":
                    sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXT)
                    sys.exit(0)
                elif c == "i":
                    opts.ignore_case = True
                    opts.smart_case = False
                elif c == "L":
                    opts.files_without_matches = True
                elif c == "l":
                    opts.files_with_matches = True
                elif c == "m":
                    try:
                        opts.max_count = int(consumed_arg)
                    except (ValueError, TypeError):
                        err_requires_arg_short(c)
                elif c == "n":
                    opts.recurse = False
                elif c == "o":
                    opts.only_matching = True
                elif c == "p":
                    opts.path_to_ignore.append(consumed_arg)
                elif c == "Q":
                    opts.literal = True
                elif c == "r":
                    opts.recurse = True
                elif c == "s":
                    opts.case_sensitive = True
                    opts.smart_case = False
                    opts.ignore_case = False
                elif c == "S":
                    opts.smart_case = True
                    opts.case_sensitive = False
                    opts.ignore_case = False
                elif c == "t":
                    opts.all_text = True
                elif c == "u":
                    opts.unrestricted = True
                elif c == "U":
                    opts.skip_vcs_ignores = True
                elif c == "v":
                    opts.invert_match = True
                elif c == "V":
                    sys.stdout.write(VERSION_TEXT)
                    sys.exit(0)
                elif c == "w":
                    opts.word_regexp = True
                elif c == "W":
                    try:
                        opts.width = int(consumed_arg)
                    except (ValueError, TypeError):
                        err_requires_arg_short(c)
                elif c == "z":
                    opts.search_zip = True
                elif c == "0":
                    opts.print0 = True
                elif c == "?":
                    sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXT)
                    sys.exit(0)
                else:
                    err_invalid_short(c)
                j += 1
            i += 1
        else:
            if pattern is None:
                pattern = a
            else:
                paths.append(a)
            i += 1

    return opts, pattern, paths

DEFAULT_IGNORES = {
    # VCS dirs that are always ignored
    ".git", ".hg", ".svn", ".bzr", "CVS", "_darcs", ".bzrignore",
}

BINARY_EXTS = {
    ".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".gif", ".bmp", ".ico", ".tiff", ".tif",
    ".pdf", ".zip", ".tar", ".gz", ".bz2", ".xz", ".7z", ".rar",
    ".exe", ".dll", ".so", ".dylib", ".o", ".obj", ".a", ".lib",
    ".class", ".jar", ".pyc", ".pyo", ".wasm",
    ".mp3", ".mp4", ".avi", ".mov", ".mkv", ".wav", ".ogg", ".flac",
    ".bin", ".iso", ".dmg",
}


def gitignore_to_regex(pattern):
    """Convert a gitignore-style pattern to a regex function.
    Returns (regex, dir_only, negate)"""
    negate = False
    if pattern.startswith("!"):
        negate = True
        pattern = pattern[1:]
    dir_only = False
    if pattern.endswith("/"):
        dir_only = True
        pattern = pattern[:-1]
    anchored = False
    if pattern.startswith("/"):
        anchored = True
        pattern = pattern[1:]
    elif "/" in pattern[:-1]:
        anchored = True
    # Build a fnmatch-style regex
    # We'll convert glob to regex manually since '/' and '**' have special meaning
    rgx = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(pattern):
        c = pattern[i]
        if c == "*":
            if i + 1 < len(pattern) and pattern[i + 1] == "*":
                # **
                rgx.append(".*")
                i += 2
                if i < len(pattern) and pattern[i] == "/":
                    i += 1
            else:
                rgx.append("[^/]*")
                i += 1
        elif c == "?":
            rgx.append("[^/]")
            i += 1
        elif c == ".":
            rgx.append(r"\.")
            i += 1
        elif c in "()+|^$@{}\\":
            rgx.append("\\" + c)
            i += 1
        else:
            rgx.append(c)
            i += 1
    regex_str = "".join(rgx)
    if anchored:
        regex_str = "^" + regex_str + "$"
    else:
        regex_str = "(^|/)" + regex_str + "$"
    try:
        return re.compile(regex_str), dir_only, negate
    except re.error:
        return None, dir_only, negate


class IgnoreSet:
    def __init__(self):
        self.patterns = []  # list of (regex, dir_only, negate)

    def add_pattern(self, pat):
        pat = pat.strip()
        if not pat or pat.startswith("#"):
            return
        compiled = gitignore_to_regex(pat)
        if compiled[0] is not None:
            self.patterns.append(compiled)

    def add_patterns(self, patterns):
        for p in patterns:
            self.add_pattern(p)

    def matches(self, relpath, is_dir):
        """Check if relpath (posix separated, relative to this ignore's root)
        matches an ignore pattern."""
        matched = False
        for regex, dir_only, negate in self.patterns:
            if dir_only and not is_dir:
                continue
            if regex.search(relpath):
                matched = not negate
        return matched


def load_ignore_file(path):
    patterns = []
    try:
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
            for line in f:
                line = line.rstrip("\n").rstrip("\r")
                if line and not line.startswith("#"):
                    patterns.append(line)
    except (IOError, OSError):
        pass
    return patterns


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Regex building
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def build_regex(pattern, opts):
    flags = 0
    if opts.literal:
        pat = re.escape(pattern)
    else:
        pat = pattern
    if opts.word_regexp:
        pat = r"\b(?:" + pat + r")\b"
    # Smart case
    case_insensitive = False
    if opts.ignore_case:
        case_insensitive = True
    elif opts.case_sensitive:
        case_insensitive = False
    elif opts.smart_case:
        # case-insensitive unless pattern contains uppercase
        if not any(c.isupper() for c in pattern):
            case_insensitive = True
    if case_insensitive:
        flags |= re.IGNORECASE
    # Multiline by default? In ag, lines are matched one at a time in practice.
    try:
        return re.compile(pat, flags)
    except re.error as e:
        sys.stderr.write("%s: error: bad regex '%s': %s\n" % (sys.argv[0], pattern, e))
        sys.exit(2)

def is_binary_data(data):
    """Heuristic: file is binary if it contains a NUL byte in first 512 bytes."""
    head = data[:512]
    return b"\x00" in head
